newsitem.title: USA: Solv-Ex says reviewed Deutsche's 13D filing.
newsitem.headline: Solv-Ex says reviewed Deutsche's 13D filing.

text.p: Solv-Ex Corp said on Friday that it is "confident" the Deutsche Bank AG will seek to minimize the effect any disposition of Solv-Ex share may have on the market.

Solv-Ex said it has reviewed Deutsche Bank's Schedule 13D filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission and it is apparent the bank's affiliates purchased a "significant amount" of Solv-Ex common shares in excess of those purchased in three transactions in January and March 1996.
In those three transactions, shares were purchased by Deutsche Bank's affiliates: Alulux Mining SA, Sandvest Petroleum SA and Russ Oil & Technology SA, Solv-Ex said.
But Solv-Ex said it has no records of any transfers between any of the bank's affiliates, or any purchase of shares by Silva Investment Ltd that are described in the filing.
Solv-Ex said it has no information as to when or how transactions occurred, or why its records differ from those in the SEC filing.

"Given the confusion and uncertainty surrounding (Deutsche Bank's) stock ownership and given the status of (Deutsche Bank) as a greater-than-10-percent shareholder of Solv-Ex, Solv-Ex is confident that (Deutsche Bank will) seek to minimize the impact any disposition of Solv-Ex shares may have on the market," the company said in a statement.

The issue arose earlier this month when Solv-Ex shareholders filed a class action lawsuit against the company and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Inc, accusing them of misrepresenting the company's business prospects, technologies and reserves.
The complaint said that, because of a series of allegedly materially false and misleading statements, the price of Solv-Ex's common stock was artificially inflated during the so-called class period.

Solv-Ex said it also is confident Deutsche Bank, as an affiliate of the company, "will comply with the legal requirements for any transfer of shares," including the registration requirements of the Securities Act of 1933 and Rule 144.
The Schedule 13D filing showed Alulux with 605,427 shares; Sandvest with 551,687; Russ Oil with 1,055,927; Silva with 750,000; and Phemex Established with 1,016,000.
In contrast, Solv-Ex said its records showed Alulux with 432,787 shares; Sandvest with 649,180; Russ Oil with 489,474; and Silva and Phemex with none.
